phase_name: Measure the redeploy checkpoint and prove a red tree is still caught

deviations.description: Record the checkpoint's total wall time on a fire that genuinely happens
deviations.reason: A full live /orchestrate cycle fire cannot be safely or appropriately self-triggered from inside an implement sub-dispatch -- cycle boundaries are owned by the orchestrator engine, not a dispatched agent. Measured the isolated component that actually changed (deploy-headless.sh's own call) instead, which fully accounts for the checkpoint's total delta since nothing else in the call chain changed.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered -- isolated component timing substituted for an end-to-end live cycle fire, with the substitution's completeness argued explicitly rather than asserted)*

deploy_headless_isolated_timing.note: Materially larger than this plan's own earlier ~50-70s estimate (carried from verify-deploy.sh's header, written under quieter ambient load). Both numbers measured on this host under the same heavy concurrent-session load documented in Phase 2/4's baseline records -- not reconciled to the header's static estimate.

live_exit_code_pair.with_skip_verify: exit=4, [deploy-headless] RESULT=landed_verify_skipped, suppression line: "Verification SUPPRESSED by --skip-verify (caller takes its own independent verification snapshot; this is NOT the same as a passed verify)."

red_tree_detectability.mechanism_tested: deploy_findings_snapshot / deploy_baseline_new_findings from lib/deploy-baseline-lib.sh, the exact functions both callers use -- entirely independent of deploy-headless.sh's own exit code
pre_findings: FINDING gate16 lean still declares routing_hard/routing_agents_hard
red_tree_detectability.injected_defect: throwaway HTML-comment line referencing "task 999999", appended to context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md, to trip the task-reference lint (gate4)
post_findings: FINDING gate16 lean still declares routing_hard/routing_agents_hard
FINDING gate3 [core] FAIL: Rule R: index-entries.json entry 'patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md' line_count mismatch (incidental source-vs-deployed drift, not a defect)
FINDING gate4 agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md:1756:<!-- TEMPORARY RED-TREE PROBE ... --> (THE INJECTED VIOLATION -- substantive catch)
FINDING gate5 core: Content differs from source: context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md (incidental source-vs-deployed drift, not a defect)
red_tree_detectability.new_findings_vs_pre: gate3, gate4, gate5 (gate4 is the substantive defect; gate3/gate5 are incidental drift from editing source without an intervening redeploy)
red_tree_detectability.revert_method: Edit tool (removed the two appended lines directly) -- NOT `git checkout --`, which guard-destructive-git.sh correctly blocked on the dirty tree per its documented 'No Destructive Git on Uncommitted Work' rule
red_tree_detectability.post_revert_confirmation: git diff --quiet -- agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md -> clean, confirmed again after this phase's final write
red_tree_detectability.conclusion: The catching mechanism never consults deploy-headless.sh's exit code at all -- it is the caller's own independent pre/post comparison. Suppressing the inline pass via --skip-verify cannot create a path where a genuinely red tree reads as green.

measurement_record.branch_contract_confirmation: Re-cited from Phase 6's own verification rather than re-derived: both predicates (-eq 1 || -eq 2, unconditional else) confirmed unedited by git diff; test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's 344-case run (Arm E = not-landed branch, checkpoint (k) = landed branch with findings) passes unchanged.
